payload.title: Experiment: gravitational field strength from a cart on a tilted track

stimulus.description: A student releases a low-friction cart from rest on a track that is tilted at an angle θ to the horizontal, and measures the acceleration of the cart down the track with a motion sensor. notes: A student releases a low-friction cart from rest on a track that is tilted at an angle θ to the horizontal, and measures the acceleration of the cart down the track with a motion sensor. The student repeats the experiment for several angles and wants to determine the gravitational field strength $g$.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe an experimental procedure to collect the data for the acceleration as a function of the angle. Include the equipment and the measurements, how the independent variable is changed, and one way to reduce the uncertainty in the measured angle.
parts.model_answer: Use a protractor (or measure the height of the raised end and the length of the track and find the angle from a trigonometric ratio) to set each angle of the track and a motion sensor to measure the acceleration; change only the angle with the same cart and track; reduce the uncertainty in the angle by measuring the height and the length with a meterstick and calculating the angle.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies a way to set and measure the angle and a way to measure the acceleration (motion sensor or a time and distance measurement)
required_elements: a way to measure the angle and a way to measure the acceleration
common_errors: omits how the acceleration is measured

rubric_rows.criterion: Changes only the angle while using the same cart and the same track (both conditions are needed)
required_elements: change only the angle with the same cart and track

rubric_rows.criterion: Reduces the uncertainty in the angle by calculating it from the height and the length measured with a meterstick, or by repeating the measurement and averaging (either earns the point)
required_elements: calculate the angle from the height and the length or repeat and average (either earns the point)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Using the relationship between the acceleration of the cart, the angle of the track, and $g$ when friction is negligible, identify the quantities that should be plotted on the vertical and horizontal axes so that the data produce a straight line whose slope can be used to find $g$.
parts.model_answer: For a frictionless incline $a=g\sin\theta$: plot $a$ on the vertical axis against $\sin\theta$ on the horizontal axis; the slope is $g$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies $a$ (vertical) versus $\sin\theta$ (horizontal)
common_errors: plots a versus theta

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: On a blank grid whose scale you choose, plot the data in a form that gives a straight line, and draw a best-fit line. Label the axes with quantities and units and use a scale that fills most of the grid.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the slope of the best-fit line using two points on the line (about 9.74 m/s^2; accept any value within 5 percent)

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the slope of the best-fit line using two points on the line (about 9.74 m/s^2; accept any value within 5 percent)
common_errors: uses data points rather than points on the line

rubric_rows.criterion: Relates the slope to the gravitational field strength: slope $=g$
common_errors: uses slope = 1/g

rubric_rows.criterion: States $g$ (about 9.7; accept any value within 8 percent) with units of meters per second squared or newtons per kilogram
alt_solutions: a value of g consistent with the student's own slope from D1

blueprint.subject: ap_physics_1
blueprint.concept: Designing an experiment and analyzing linearized data to extract the gravitational field strength from a low-friction incline
student_thinking: Describe the measurements and how uncertainty in the angle is reduced
Linearize the incline relationship and plot the data
Use the slope to determine g

key_conditions.condition: the generated accelerations follow $a=g\sin\theta$ with a small random error so the best-fit slope is within a few percent of g
key_conditions.evidence: the code rejects a seed whose fitted g differs from 9.8 by more than four percent

verification.independent_path: the slope is recomputed from the normal equations with numpy linalg.solve and compared with polyfit; the fitted g is compared with the reference value

parts.label: A
accepted_answers: Use a protractor (or measure the height of the raised end and the length of the track and find the angle from a trigonometric ratio) to set each angle of the track and a motion sensor to measure the acceleration; change only the angle with the same cart and track; reduce the uncertainty in the angle by measuring the height and the length with a meterstick and calculating the angle.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies a way to set and measure the angle and a way to measure the acceleration (motion sensor or a time and distance measurement)
elements: a way to measure the angle and a way to measure the acceleration

rubric_rows.criterion: Changes only the angle while using the same cart and the same track (both conditions are needed)
elements: change only the angle with the same cart and track

rubric_rows.criterion: Reduces the uncertainty in the angle by calculating it from the height and the length measured with a meterstick, or by repeating the measurement and averaging (either earns the point)
elements: calculate the angle from the height and the length or repeat and average (either earns the point)

parts.label: B
accepted_answers: For a frictionless incline $a=g\sin\theta$: plot $a$ on the vertical axis against $\sin\theta$ on the horizontal axis; the slope is $g$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies $a$ (vertical) versus $\sin\theta$ (horizontal)
Axes are labeled with quantities and units (sin theta has no units) and the scale fills most of the grid
Plots the five points $(\sin\theta, a)$ accurately
Draws a straight best-fit line through the trend of the points

parts.label: D
accepted_answers: The slope of the best-fit line is $g\approx 9.7\text{ m/s}^2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the slope of the best-fit line using two points on the line (about 9.74 m/s^2; accept any value within 5 percent)
Relates the slope to the gravitational field strength: slope $=g$
States $g$ (about 9.7; accept any value within 8 percent) with units of meters per second squared or newtons per kilogram

review.summary: The item has no instant-reject condition, but it fails on key/scoring and exam suitability. Row A2 awards a point for "same cart and same track", which the prompt never asks for. Row D1 is chained to C3, so a student who misses C3 is penalized twice. The reference slope (9.74) differs from the independent solver's (9.85), though the 5% tolerance covers both. At an estimated 27 minutes with hand plotting, the task load is heavy.

scope_skill.notes: Parts A and B fit skill 3.A. Parts C and D are graphing and slope calculation (1.B, 2.D), which is acceptable within the bundle. The 10-point weight matches the Experimental Design and Analysis type.

key_scoring.notes: Row A2 requires "same cart and track", but the prompt asks only for equipment, measurements, how the independent variable is changed, and one way to reduce angle uncertainty. Row D1 depends on C3, so an earlier graphing error is penalized again. The reference slope of 9.74 versus the solver's 9.85 is covered by the 5% tolerance.

stimulus_expression.notes: The data table is complete and the wording is clear. The stimulus text is duplicated in notes, which is minor.

distractor_explanation.notes: Not applicable to an FRQ. The rubric's common-error entries are thin, with none for A2 or A3.

exam_suitability.notes: The estimated 27 minutes is heavy because part C requires plotting five points by hand. The design part (A) is generic.

difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: This is a standard AP Physics 1 lab-design and linearization item. The student must apply Newton's second law along an incline (a = g sinθ), design a procedure, choose a linearized plot (a vs sinθ), then plot and read the slope. The reasoning is multi-step but routine, and each step is within Unit 2 scope. The representation changes are a table of angles to sinθ values, then to a graph, then to a slope. The data are clean (a = 9.8 sinθ) and need only five sinθ values and one slope calculation, so the arithmetic is light. The reading load is modest and the wording is unambiguous. Difficulty comes from the intended levers: choosing the governing law, linearizing, and experimental design. This matches a full-mock lab free-response question.
